name: seatbelt
phrases: Pull your seatbelt slowly, it slides. **Yank it, it locks.**
Pull your seatbelt slowly and it slides. Yank it, and it locks.
Here's the little machine **inside the reel.**
Here's the little machine hiding inside the reel.
The belt is stored on a **spring-loaded reel** called a retractor.
The belt is stored on a spring-loaded reel, called a retractor.
The spring keeps the belt **taut,** so you can still move around.
The spring keeps the belt taut, so you can still move around freely.
Each end of the spool has **ratchet teeth.**
Each end of the spool has a ring of ratchet teeth.
Beside them waits a **locking pawl.**
Right beside them waits a locking pawl.
When the pawl catches a tooth, the belt **can't come out.**
When the pawl catches a tooth, the reel locks, and the belt can't come out.
So what moves the pawl? **Two sensors.**
So what moves the pawl? There are two kinds of sensor.
Sensor one: a **pendulum.**
Sensor one is a pendulum.
Brake hard, and it **swings** away from plumb.
Brake hard, or roll over, and it swings away from plumb.
That swing drives the pawl into the teeth. **The reel locks.**
That swing drives the pawl into the teeth, and the reel locks.
Sensor two watches the belt: a **centrifugal clutch.**
Sensor two watches the belt itself. It's a centrifugal clutch.
Pull slowly, and the belt pays out. **Jerk it, and the reel locks.**
Pull the belt slowly, and it pays out. Jerk it fast, and the clutch locks the reel.
Many newer cars add a **pretensioner:** a small charge that removes slack.
Many newer cars also add a pretensioner. In a crash, a small charge tightens the belt to remove slack.
The modern three-point belt: **Nils Bohlin, for Volvo, 1959.**
The modern three-point belt was developed by Nils Bohlin for Volvo, and introduced in 1959.
Next time your belt snaps tight, you'll know **what just happened.**
Next time your belt snaps tight on a hard stop, you'll know what just happened.
